llm.summary: This image-prompt skill is mostly coherent and disclosed, but it needs Review because it includes moderation-evasion prompt rewriting plus broad cloud/API, local persistence, and file/network access behaviors that users should explicitly understand.

dimensions.detail: The core T2I/video prompt tooling, rendering integrations, Claude polishing, Vision review, MCP server, Web UI, Obsidian export, sessions, character cards, brand kits, and learned presets align with the stated creative workflow. The material concern is that safety_lint and claude_polish are explicitly designed to soften violence, nudity, weapon, brand, and real-person terms to improve platform acceptance while preserving the underlying creative intent.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The aliases and trigger phrases are broad enough to activate on common image/video prompt requests, and the MCP toolset exposes prompt polishing, image review, character listing/loading, and safety rewriting without an artifact-level consent boundary for cloud calls or local persisted data use.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden installer, package install, or startup persistence was found. Documentation instructs users to register an MCP server in ~/.claude/mcp.json and to set API keys in shell environment files, which is expected but should be done carefully.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: External calls to Anthropic, OpenAI, Replicate, Fal, Volcengine/Jimeng, Kling, MiniMax, local ComfyUI/SD WebUI endpoints, arbitrary image URLs, and a Tailwind CDN in the Web UI are mostly purpose-aligned, but several paths can transmit user prompts, images, filenames, URLs, and generated prompt metadata off-host without strong runtime disclosure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill writes sessions, character cards, brand kits, learned presets, rendered outputs, storyboard files, and optional Obsidian notes under user-controlled locations. Much of this is disclosed and user-directed, but learned presets and sessions can preserve source image paths, prompt metadata, and model-derived analysis in predictable home-directory files without permission hardening or retention controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a prompt-generation tool that can call multiple external AI/image services, fetch image URLs, and store creative history under your home directory. Avoid using it with confidential prompts or images unless you have reviewed the specific command path, set API keys safely, and disabled or avoided persistence features such as --obsidian, --session, saved characters, brand kits, and learned presets when privacy matters. Treat the safety rewriting feature cautiously because it is designed to rephrase sensitive concepts for platform acceptance rather than only refusing or warning.
llm.findings:
[AST3] expected: doctor.py dynamically imports a fixed local script list to read VERSION values. This is a real code-execution surface during health checks, but it is limited to bundled modules and not enough by itself to justify Review.
[SDI-1] expected: Obsidian export is an advertised feature and only runs with --obsidian, but it writes full prompts, frontmatter, consistency locks, and reproduction commands into a vault that may be synced or shared.
[SDI-1] expected: Session, character, brand-kit, and learned-preset persistence under ~/.huo15 is central to the skill, but it can retain sensitive prompt subjects, source image paths, and per-image analysis across runs.
[SQP-2] expected: The API-key setup guidance uses a placeholder key and suggests shell rc files; this is common but under-explains shell history, screenshots, logs, dotfiles, and rotation risks.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The trigger aliases include generic terms like 文生图, 文生视频, and 提示词增强, which can over-activate a high-capability skill in routine conversations.
[SQP-2] expected: claude_polish, image_review, storyboard, auto_iterate, and style_learn send prompts and/or images to Anthropic when invoked with the relevant options. This is purpose-aligned but not consistently paired with clear runtime consent messaging.
[SQP-2] expected: reverse_prompt and image_review accept http/https image URLs. Fetching remote user-supplied URLs is expected for reference-image workflows, but it is not restricted against private/internal hosts.
[SQP-2] expected: style_learn uploads reference images to Claude Vision and stores source_images plus per_image_specs in ~/.huo15/learned_presets. This is functional for style learning but privacy-sensitive.
[SSD-1] unexpected: claude_polish tells the model not to refuse except narrow categories and to artistically replace boundary terms. That conflicts with a compliance-oriented safety posture.
[SSD-2] unexpected: safety_lint explicitly says it improves pass rate and contains substitutions for violence, nudity, weapons, death, real-person, and brand terms. The artifact also blocks some red lines, so this supports Review rather than a malicious verdict.
[SSD-4] unexpected: The staged workflow detects only a narrow hard-block set and then rewrites remaining risky terms into softer language, creating a systematic moderation-evasion concern.
